column1: # DocID 11214358 — THE DOCUMENT THIS ARCHIVE HAS BEEN GUESSING ABOUT FOR THREE DAYS, READ.
# Arolsen Archives, opened 20 September 2026 with David's consent declaration ticked.
# THE BACKGROUND, BECAUSE THE CORRECTION IS THE POINT. On 17 September the index showed that Jacob
# Leibholz (b. 08.08.1884), Auguste "Lizzy" Leibholz née Luwwinsky (b. 28.08.1893) and Kurt Luwinski
# (b. 11.05.1912) ALL CARRY THE SAME DocID, 11214358, in a series the catalogue calls "Deportations
# and Transports". This archive wrote that the likeliest reading was "a deportation form that records
# a man's household and his next of kin", and called that reading "evidence instead of the charitable
# guess". IT WAS STILL A GUESS, AND ON THE DOCUMENT TYPE IT WAS WRONG.

*** WHAT THE DOCUMENT ACTUALLY IS ***
column2: NOT A DEPORTATION FORM. It is a BERLIN RESIDENTS' REGISTRATION CARD — signature 1.2.1.5, "Berlin: Registration Cards from Jewish Residents", filed under 1.2.1 Deportations and Transports, Part 24, folder "MFN01335", reference 10000375 24. Printed form "Vordruck Nr. 25 B". The series name is what misled the reading; the series name is not the document.

column1: *** AND IT IS TWO IMAGES, NOT ONE ***
column2: image 001 is the Leibholz family's card. IMAGE 002 IS A RULED LIST OF SURNAMES AND BIRTH DATES. One DocID covers both, which is why eleven people index to it. *** LATER THE SAME DAY THE SECOND SHEET WAS IDENTIFIED: IT IS THE HOUSE LIST FOR MERANER STRASSE 2. *** The 1939 census database, searched by street and house number rather than by name, puts ANNA PUFF, BORN 1 JUNE 1895, at MERANER STRASSE 2 — and PUFF, Anna, 06/01/1895 is one of the eleven names indexed on this DocID. That is what the stamp on image 001 says it should be: "Lt. Hausliste 1945 n. erfaßt". ONE EXACT MATCH OUT OF SEVEN UNPLACED NAMES, and the other six would not be in that database at all if they were not Jewish, so it is a strong reading rather than a proof. See data/jacob-leibholz-deportation.tsv.

column1: the eleven indexed persons
column2: SCHMIDT Else 11.06.1903 · PUFF Anna 01.06.1895 · HEINICKE Anna 08.01.1897 · LEIBHOLZ Auguste née LUWWINSKY 28.08.1893 · LEIBHOLZ Jacques Jaques 08.08.1884 · LUWINSKI Kurt 11.05.1912 · HERZOG Else 07.12.1902 · BIERE Henriette 15.09.1891 · KOCH Erika 09.02.1904 · LEIBHOLZ Siegfried 05.08.1925 · NICKSCH Klara 23.04.1906.

column1: *** WHERE KURT IS, AND IT IS NOT WHERE THE GUESS PUT HIM ***
column2: KURT IS NOT ON THE FAMILY'S CARD. Image 001 lists three people and he is not one of them. The line that carries his birth date is on IMAGE 002, among Herzog, Heinicke, Nicksch, Schmidt and Puff — the sheet of other households. It reads as "Luwinski Kurt 11.5.12"; the surname is faint and only the date is beyond argument.

column1: so the earlier reading is withdrawn in part
column2: WITHDRAWN: that the document is a deportation form, and that it names Kurt "as next of kin on a form about his father". STANDS: that the three share one DocID, which was always a hard fact from the index; and that neither Kurt nor Auguste was deported. WHAT REPLACES IT: the shared DocID is a consequence of two unrelated sheets being scanned under one number, and Kurt's appearance is on the second sheet, in a list this archive cannot yet explain.

column1: IMAGE 001, LINE BY LINE — the head of the card
column2: Surname LEIBHOLZ. Beruf (occupation): one word, not confidently read. Staatsangehörigkeit: "Pr" — Preußen.

column2: AUGUSTE geb. LUWWINSKY · 28.8.93 · GEBURTSORT SAUERBAUM · with a later annotation dated 18.1.44 giving a street and number.

column1: line 3
column2: Kind: SIEGFRIED · 5.?.25 · BERLIN-SCHÖNEBERG. The month digit is not legible on this scan; the Arolsen index gives 5 AUGUST 1925 and the family tree gives only the year 1925. THE INDEX IS TAKEN AS THE BETTER READING AND THE CARD IS NOT CLAIMED TO CONFIRM IT.

column1: *** WHAT IS NEW AND CHECKS OUT ***
column2: AUGUSTE'S BIRTHPLACE IN HER OWN HOUSEHOLD'S HANDWRITING: SAUERBAUM. Mapping the Lives gave "born Sauerbaum/Rössel" from the 1939 census card. A Berlin registration card written by a different hand for a different purpose says the same word. Two independent sources, one village in Kreis Rössel, East Prussia — the village her mother JOHANNA THIMM came from.

column1: and a smaller precision on Siegfried, stated smaller than it first was
column2: the card gives BERLIN-SCHÖNEBERG. *** THIS FILE FIRST SAID THAT WAS A BIRTHPLACE "NOTHING ELSE DID" GIVE. THAT IS WRONG AND IS WITHDRAWN. *** Mapping the Lives already had him as "Leibholz, Siegfried, * 05.08.1925 in Berlin", read on 20 September and recorded in data/mappingthelives-leibholz.tsv, and the Arolsen index gives the same date. WHAT THE CARD ADDS IS THE DISTRICT AND NOTHING MORE: Berlin-Schöneberg, which is the family's own street. It is the MyHeritage tree that has him as 1925-2005 with no day and no place, not this archive.

column1: the address history, and what a second attempt got out of it
column2: the Wohnungen column runs down the right of the card with a dated run of Berlin addresses. IT IS STILL NOT TRANSCRIBED and on this scan it cannot be. Tried again on 20 September with median-filtered denoising, five-times and seven-times upscaling and unsharp masking: the sharpening amplifies the film grain into the hand and destroys it, and the gentler pass leaves words that can be guessed at and not read. *** AND THERE IS ONLY ONE SCAN. *** Six URL variants were tested against the image server — the H, V and L partitions, a _big suffix and a .tif — and all five alternatives return 404. The 976-pixel frame is what exists.

column1: what IS legible in that column, and it is only this
column2: A RUN OF DATES BEGINNING IN 1913 — three entries read as 18.13, 19.13 and 21.13, one as 23/4.15, and further entries below — with the latest annotation on the card being AUGUSTE'S 18.1.44. THE STREET NAMES ARE NOT READABLE. This archive is not going to publish a Berlin address it guessed at from a grey microfilm frame; it has been wrong twice this fortnight by reading a good fit as a finding.

column1: the stamp at the foot
column2: Lt. Hausliste 1945 n. erfaßt — according to the house list of 1945, not recorded. That is a post-war annotation on a wartime card, and it is the reason the card survives in this series at all.
